beats: Hook: millions of requests begin with the same system prompt; why compute it again for every one? (line_prefix_same_speech).

Sharing patterns (slide 28, taped): few-shot examples (line_prefix_examples_board), self-consistency (many answers to one question), multi-turn chat where every turn repeats the history (line_prefix_chat_stack, line_round_table), tree of thought.

vLLM already shared prefix blocks inside one batch (L13-03), but a request's cache died with it; SGLang keeps it alive for later requests (her words: 'one request is dead... we may still want to keep it') (line_paged_shared_coat, planned for L13-03).

RadixAttention (SGLang, NeurIPS 2024; slides 29-31): every request's KV cache in one radix tree (a compressed trie, her LeetCode aside); a new request walks down the longest matching branch and computes only its new tip; nodes split where conversations part (line_prefix_tree_tags or line_prefix_rail_junctions; red pen marks new / hit / evicted).
A cache hit, in the cloakroom: the clerk already has the bundle for that beginning (line_prefix_lookup_drawer).
LRU eviction (slide 29): when memory runs out, cut the leaf used longest ago that no live request is on (line_prefix_gardener_prune).

Zero-overhead scheduler (slide 32): the tree matching runs on the CPU; it prepares the next batch while the GPU runs this one; the price: a finished request's memory is freed one iteration late (line_prefix_next_tray_ready).

vLLM vs SGLang (slide 33): no new fragmentation, because tree nodes hold whole blocks (line_paged_crates_on_demand, planned for L13-03); vLLM now does automatic prefix caching by hashing blocks; both do chunked prefill and disaggregation.

Mooncake (Qin et al., FAST 2025, Best Paper; slide 34): one big cluster shares a distributed KV pool, with CPU memory and SSDs behind the GPUs, so a hit can come from another machine (line_prefix_shared_warehouse).
Takeaway: compute a beginning once and keep it while it stays popular.

drawings.prompt: The clerk (an invented cheerful clerk: simple round face, dot eyes, short tousled hair, a pencil tucked behind one ear, a collared shirt with rolled-up sleeves under a bib apron) sits at a desk, seen from the front, tiredly copying out by hand the same long page yet again, with heavy eyelids and a slumped back; the page is covered only in wavy pen lines, not letters. Beside the desk stand three tall wobbly towers of identical finished pages. In front of the desk, on the right, a long queue of invented guests (simple round faces, dot eyes; different hairstyles: round glasses, a ponytail, a cap, curls, a bob, a bun) wait their turn, and every one of them holds up the same rolled-up blank scroll. Landscape image 1536x1024; everything fills about 92% of the width and about 80% of the height. The scrolls are blank. No text, no letters, no numbers, no symbols, no logos anywhere.

drawings.name: line_prefix_tree_tags
drawings.prompt: A single tree drawn clearly, like a picture-book illustration, seen from the front: one thick trunk rises from a small mound at the bottom and splits into three main branches; each main branch splits again into two or three smaller branches, and some of those split once more, giving about nine twig ends in all, well spread out. From the end of every twig hangs one small blank paper tag on a short string. The bark is drawn with only a few simple lines; no foliage except two or three small leaves near each tag; no birds, no ground details, no background. Portrait image 1024x1536; the tree fills about 88% of the width and about 90% of the height. The tags are blank. No text, no letters, no numbers, no symbols, no logos anywhere.

drawings.name: line_prefix_rail_junctions
drawings.prompt: A railway seen from straight above, a bird's-eye view like a model railway: one single track enters at the bottom centre and runs up the picture; at three junctions with switch points it splits, branch after branch, into six tracks that fan out towards the top. Small simple trains sit on the tracks: a long train on the shared main line coming up from the bottom, and a short train waiting at the end of three of the branches. Portrait image 1024x1536; the tracks fill about 85% of the width and about 90% of the height. No signals with writing, no station signs. No text, no letters, no numbers, no symbols, no logos anywhere.

drawings.name: line_prefix_gardener_prune
drawings.prompt: An invented gardener (simple round face, dot eyes, a wide sun hat, gardening gloves, an apron with pockets) stands on a small step ladder and snips off one dry, drooping twig at the end of a branch with garden shears; on that twig hangs an old, curled paper tag with a small cobweb on it. The rest of the branch carries fresh twigs, each with a crisp new blank tag, which the gardener carefully leaves alone. A small basket on the ground below already holds a few cut dry twigs. Square image 1024x1024; the gardener, the ladder and the branch fill about 85% of the width and about 85% of the height. The tags are blank. No text, no letters, no numbers, no symbols, no logos anywhere.

drawings.name: line_prefix_chat_stack
drawings.prompt: Four stacks of paper sheets stand side by side on a long table, seen from the front, evenly spaced from left to right and growing like a staircase: the first stack is a short pile of sheets; the second is the very same pile plus one new sheet on top; the third has one more again; the fourth one more again.
